hook: Why do credit cards have sixteen digits?

blocks.narration: Why do credit cards have sixteen digits? They are not random. Every single digit has a job, starting with the very first one.
blocks.visual: A neat row of sixteen small glowing clay beads floating above an open clay wallet on a dark blue table, nothing printed anywhere

blocks.narration: A four means Visa, a five usually means Mastercard. The first six to eight digits name the bank that issued your card.
blocks.visual: Four tiny clay bank buildings standing on a dark blue table, each one lighting up in turn, glowing beads drifting between them

blocks.narration: The middle digits are your account, and the final digit is a math check that catches typos. Next time someone asks you
blocks.visual: A tiny clay magnifying glass inspecting the last bead in a row of glowing clay beads, that last bead glowing bright green

cta: Follow for more everyday things explained.

captions.hook_line: Why do credit cards have 16 digits? Every digit has a job 💳
captions.body: The first digit names the network, the first 6 to 8 identify the bank that issued the card, the middle is your account, and the last is a Luhn check digit that catches typos.
captions.share_line: Send this to someone who reads card numbers out loud.

sources.claim: Card number structure and issuer identification
